Runtime provider probe — reads `provider-probe.json` and returns the best\n//! provider for each NOAA model (GFS, HRRR, NBM, …).\n//!\n//! The probe file is written by `xtask probe-providers`. Providers should be re-probed in three cases:\n//! 1. **File absent**: `ProviderProbe::load` returns `Err`\n//! 2. **File stale**: `is_fresh()` returns `false` (timestamp > 24h old)\n//! 3. **Consecutive HTTP errors**: `ProviderFailureTracker::should_reprobe()` returns `true`\n//!\n//! The `ProviderFailureTracker` from `gribtract_fetch` tracks consecutive\n//! HTTP failures per provider at runtime. Use it alongside the staleness check:\n//!\n//! # Example\n//!\n//! This example shows the complete runtime provider selection workflow with\n//! re-probe triggers for staleness and consecutive HTTP errors:\n//!\n//! ```no_run\n//! use gribtract::ProviderProbe;\n//! use gribtract_fetch::probe::ProviderFailureTracker;\n//! use std::path::Path;\n//!\n//! // Load provider probe results\n//! let probe = match ProviderProbe::load(Path::new(\"provider-probe.json\")) {\n//! Err(_) => {\n//!         // Case 1: File absent — trigger re-probe\n//!         eprintln!(\"provider-probe.json not found, running initial probe...\");\n//!         run_probe_and_write_json(); // Your implementation\n//!         return;\n//!     }\n//! };\n//!\n//! // Initialize failure tracker (threshold = 3 consecutive errors)\n//! let tracker = ProviderFailureTracker::default_threshold();\n//!\n//! // Check if we should re-probe (Case 2 OR Case 3)\n//! // is_valid() checks both: file staleness AND consecutive failures\n//! if !probe.is_valid(24 * 3600, &tracker) {\n//!     // Get specific providers that need re-probing for logging\n//!     let needing = probe.providers_needing_reprobe(&tracker);\n//!\n//!     if !probe.is_fresh(24 * 3600) {\n//!         eprintln!(\"provider-probe.json is stale (>24h old), triggering re-probe...\");\n//!     }\n//!\n//!     if !needing.is_empty() {\n//!         eprintln!(\"Re-probe triggered by consecutive failures: {}\",\n//!             needing.join(\", \"));\n//!     }\n//!\n//!     run_probe_and_write_json(); // Your implementation\n//!     return;\n//! }\n//!\n//! // Safe to use cached provider rankings\n//! if let Some(provider) = probe.best_provider(\"gfs\") {\n//!     println!(\"Best GFS provider: {provider}\");\n//!\n//!     // After HTTP requests, record success/failure\n//!     match fetch_data_from_provider(provider).await {\n//!  let (y, m) = if m <= 2 { (y - 1, m + 9) } else { (y, m - 3) };\n    let era = if y >= 0 { y } else { y - 399 } / 400;\n    let yoe = y - era * 400; // [0, 399]\n    let doy = (153 * m as i64 + 2) / 5 if days < days_in_year as i64 {\n                break;\n            }\n            days -= days_in_year as i64;\n            year += 1;\n        }\n\n        // Now 'days' is the day-of-year fn is_leap_year(year: i32) -> bool {\n        (year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0) || (year % 400 == 0)\n    }\n\n    fn day_of_year_to_md(day_of_year: u32, year: i32) -> (u32, u32) {\n        let days_in_month = if is_leap_year(year) {\n            [0, 31, 29, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31]\n        } else {\n            [0, 31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31]\n        };\n\n        let mut day = day_of_year + 1; // 1-indexed\n        let mut month = 1;\n\n        while month <= 12 && day > days_in_month[month as usize] {\n            day -= days_in_month[month as usize];\n            month += 1;\n        }\n\n        (month, day)\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn ymd_to_days_known() {\n        // 1970-01-01 = day 0\n        assert_eq!(ymd_to_days(1970, 1, 1), Content-Range header information\n70\t#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\n71\tpub struct ContentRange {\n72\t    /// Start byte position\n73\t    pub start: u64,\n74\t    /// End byte position (inclusive)\n75\t value\n82\t    ///\n83\t    /// Format: `bytes start-end/total` or `bytes */total` or `bytes start-end/*`\n84\t    pub fn parse(header: &str) -> Result<Self> {\n85\t        let header = header.trim();\n86\t        if !header.starts_with(\"bytes \") {\n87\t            return Err(FetchError::InvalidContentRange(format!(\n88\t                \"Missing 'bytes' prefix: {}\",\n89\t                header\n90\t            )));\n91\t        }\n92\t\n93\t        let parts: Vec<&str> = header[6..].split('/').collect();\n94\t        if parts.len() != 2 {\n95\t            return Err(FetchError::InvalidContentRange(format!(\n96\t                \"Invalid format: {}\",\n97\t                header\n98\t            )));\n99\t        }\n100\t\n101\t        let total = match parts[1] {\n102\t            \"*\" => None,\n103\t            s => Some(\n104\t                s.parse::<u64>()\n105\t                    .map_err(|_| FetchError::InvalidContentRange(format!(\"Invalid total: {}\", s)))?,\n106\t            ),\n107\t        };\n108\t\n109\t        if parts[0] == \"*\" {\n110\t            return Ok(ContentRange {\n111\t                start: 0,\n112\t                end: 0,\n113\t                total,\n114\t            });\n115\t        }\n116\t\n117\t        let range_parts: Vec<&str> = parts[0].split('-').collect();\n118\t        if range_parts.len() != 2 {\n119\t            return Err(FetchError::InvalidContentRange(format!(\n120\t                \"Invalid range format: {}\",\n121\t                header\n122\t            )));\n123\t        }\n124\t\n125\t        let start = range_parts[0]\n126\t            .parse::<u64>()\n127\t            .map_err(|_| FetchError::InvalidContentRange(format!(\"Invalid start: {}\", range_parts[0])))?;\n128\t        let end = range_parts[1]\n129\t            .parse::<u64>()\n130\t            .map_err(|_| FetchError::InvalidContentRange(format!(\"Invalid end: {}\", range_parts[1])))?;\n131\t\n132\t        Ok(ContentRange { start, end, total })\n133\t    }\n134\t\n135\t    /// Get the length of this range\n136\t    pub fn length(&self) -> u64 {\n137\t        self.end - self.start + 1\n138\t    }\n139\t}\n140\t\n141\t/// HTTP client for fetching GRIB2 data via byte-range requests\n142\t#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\n143\tpub struct FetchClient {\n144\t the URL.\n162\t    fn extract_provider_from_url(url: &str) -> Option<String> {\n163\t        let url = url.to_lowercase();\n164\t\n165\t        // NOAA S3 buckets: https://noaa-{bucket}.s3.amazonaws.com/\n166\t        if url.contains(\"s3.amazonaws.com\") {\n167\t            if url.contains(\"hrrr\") {\n168\t                return Some(\"s3:hrrr\".to_string());\n169\t            } else if url.contains(\"gefs\") {\n170\t                return Some(\"s3:gefs\".to_string());\n171\t            } else if url.contains(\"nbm\") {\n172\t                return Some(\"s3:nbm\".to_string());\n173\t            } else if url.contains(\"gfs\") {\n174\t                return Some(\"s3:gfs\".to_string());\n175\t            }\n176\t        }\n177\t\n178\t        // Google Cloud Storage: https://storage.googleapis.com/{bucket}/\n179\t        if url.contains(\"storage.googleapis.com\") {\n180\t            if url.contains(\"high-resolution-rapid-refresh\") || url.contains(\"hrrr\") {\n181\t                return Some(\"gcs:hrrr\".to_string());\n182\t            } else if     .build()\n208\t            .expect(\"Failed to build HTTP client\");\n209\t\n210\t        Self {\n211\t            client,\n212\t            default_timeout: timeout,\n213\t /// Fetch a byte range from a URL\n229\t    pub async fn fetch_range(&mut self, url: &str, range: RangeRequest) -> Result<RangeResponse> {\n230\t        let provider =     data,\n281\t                    content_range,\n282\t                    total_size,\n283\t                })\n284\t            }\n285\t            Err(e) => {\n286\t                // Record async fn probe_url_inner(&mut self, url: &str) -> Result<ProbeInnerResult, crate::FetchError> {\n205\t        let _start = std::time::Instant::now();\n206\t\n207\t        // Use the client's probe requests are supported\n212\t        let supports_range = probe_info.supports_range;\n213\t\n214\t        // Get content length\n215\t        let content_length = };\n225\t\n226\t        let ttfb = range_start.elapsed();\n227\t\n228\t        let throughput_mbs = if let Some(resp) = range_response {\n229\t            let bytes = resp.data.len() as f64;\n230\t            let seconds = ttfb.as_secs_f64();\n231\t            (bytes / seconds) / (1024.0 * 1024.0)\n232\t        } else {\n233\t            0.0\n234\t        };\n235\t\n236\t        Ok(ProbeInnerResult {\n237\t            connect_time,\n238\t            ttfb,\n239\t            throughput_mbs,\n240\t        })\n241\t    }\n242\t\n243\t    /// Calculate a combined score for provider selection\n244\t        let ttfb_penalty = result.ttfb.as_millis() as f64;\n249\t        let throughput_penalty = if result.throughput_mbs > 0.0 {\n250\t            1000.0 / result.throughput_mbs\n251\t        } else fresh results\n        let results = ProviderProbeResults {\n            models: std::collections::HashMap::new(),\n            timestamp: chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339(),\n            git_sha: None,\n        };\n\n        // Simulate consecutive HTTP errors for a provider\n        // Initially is_valid should return true\n        assert!(probe.is_valid(&results, Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600)),\n                \"is_valid should return true initially with no failures\");\n\n        // First HTTP error\n        probe.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n false after 2 failures\");\n        assert!(probe.is_valid(&results, Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600)),\n                \"is_valid should still be true after 2 failures\");\n\n        // Third HTTP error - this should trigger reprobe\n        probe.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n        assert!(probe.should_reprobe(\"s3:hrrr\"), \"should_reprobe should be true after 3 failures\");\n        assert!(!probe.is_valid(&results, Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600)),\n                \"is_valid should be false after 3 consecutive failures\");\n\n        // Verify the consecutive error counter is being tracked correctly\n        assert_eq!(probe.failure_count(\"s3:hrrr\"), 3, \"failure count should be 3\");\n\n        // Simulate a successful request - should reset the counter\n        probe.record_success(\"s3:hrrr\");\n        assert_eq!(probe.failure_count(\"s3:hrrr\"), 0, \"failure count should be reset to 0\");\n        assert!(!probe.should_reprobe(\"s3:hrrr\"), should_reprobe is true\n        // (dual-trigger logic: stale OR should_reprobe)\n\n        // Test 1: Fresh results, no failures - should be valid\n        let fresh_results = ProviderProbeResults {\n            models: std::collections::HashMap::new(),\n            timestamp: chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339(),\n            git_sha: None,\n        };\n        assert!(probe.is_valid(&fresh_results, Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600)),\n                \"Fresh results with no failures should be valid\");\n\n        // Test 2: Stale results, no failures - should be invalid (staleness trigger)\n        let stale_results = ProviderProbeResults {\n            models: std::collections::HashMap::new(),\n            timestamp: (chrono::Utc::now() - chrono::Duration::hours(25)).to_rfc3339(),\n            git_sha: None,\n        };\n        assert!(!probe.is_valid(&stale_results, Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600)),\n                \"Stale results should be invalid even with no failures\");\n\n        // Test 3: Fresh results, with failures - should be invalid (should_reprobe trigger)\n        probe.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n        probe.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n        probe.record_failure(\"s3:hrrr\");\n        assert!(!probe.is_valid(&fresh_results, Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600)),\n                \"Fresh results with failures should be invalid\");\n\n        // Test 4: Stale results, with failures - should be invalid (both triggers)\n        assert!(!probe.is_valid(&stale_results, Duration::from_secs(24 * 3600)),\n                \"Stale results with failures should be invalid (both triggers active)\");\n\n        // Test 5: Fresh results, with failures below threshold - should be valid\n        let Probe File Generation (Startup/Re-probe)\n\n**File:** `xtask/src/probe_providers.rs`\n\n**Function:** `run()`\n\n**Purpose:** Generates `provider-probe.json` by probing all providers for all models\n\n**Selection Logic:** \n- Probes each `(model, provider)` pair\n- Measures head latency and throughput\n- Computes score: `head_latency_ms + 1000.0 / max(throughput_mbs, 0.001)`\n- Ranks providers per model by ascending score\n\n**`should_reprobe` Integration:** \n- ❌ NOT APPLICABLE - This is the initial probing that creates the cache, not runtime selection\n- This is what gets triggered when `should_reprobe` returns true\n\n---\n\n### 2. Probe File Load (Runtime)\n\n**File:** `crates/gribtract/src/provider_probe.rs`\n\n**Key Functions:**\n\n- `ProviderProbe::load(path)` - Loads `provider-probe.json` from disk\n- `ProviderProbe::is_fresh(max_age_secs)` - Checks if probe timestamp is fresh\n- `ProviderProbe::is_valid(max_age_secs, tracker)` - **✅ CHECKS `should_reprobe`**\n- `ProviderProbe::providers_needing_reprobe(tracker)` - Returns providers needing re-probe\n- `ProviderProbe::best_provider(model)` - Returns best provider for model\n- `ProviderProbe::ranked_providers(model)` - Returns all providers ranked\n\n**Selection Logic:**\n- Reads pre-computed rankings from `provider-probe.json`\n- Returns first provider in ranking (best score) via `best_provider()`\n- Does NOT re-evaluate providers at selection time\n\n**`should_reprobe` Integration:** \n- ✅ **FULLY INTEGRATED** in `is_valid()` (lines 184-200)\n- ✅ Checks both staleness AND consecutive failures via `ProviderFailureTracker`\n- ✅ Returns `false` if either staleness check fails OR `tracker.should_reprobe()` returns true for any provider\n- ✅ `providers_needing_reprobe()` provides detailed list for logging\n\n---\n\n### 3. Runtime Provider Selection (Before Fetch)\n\n**File:** `crates/gribtract-fetch/src/probe.rs`\n\n**Key Functions:**\n\n- `ProviderProbe::get_best_provider(results, model)` - Returns best provider from probe results\n- `ProviderProbe::is_valid(results, max_age)` - **✅ CHECKS `should_reprobe`**\n- `ProviderProbe::is_stale(results, max_age)` - Checks staleness only\n- `ProviderProbe::providers_needing_reprobe()` - Returns providers needing re-probe\n\n**Selection Logic:**\n- Selects first successful provider from probe results\n- Does NOT apply runtime failure filtering at selection time\n- Relies on pre-validation via `is_valid()` before selection\n\n**`should_reprobe` Integration:** \n- ✅ **FULLY INTEGRATED** in `is_valid()` (lines 361-376)\n- ✅ Calls `Self::is_stale()` first, then checks consecutive failures\n- ✅ Iterates through `consecutive_failures` and calls `should_reprobe()` for each\n- ✅ Returns `false` if any provider has exceeded the threshold\n- ⚠️ **NOT INTEGRATED** in `get_best_provider()` - assumes validation happened before\n\n---\n\n### 4. HTTP Client Execution (During Fetch)\n\n**File:** `crates/gribtract-fetch/src/client.rs`\n\n**Key Functions:**\n\n- `FetchClient::fetch_range(&mut self, url, range)` - Fetch byte range\n- `FetchClient::fetch_all(&mut self, url)` - Fetch entire resource\n- `FetchClient::resource_size(&mut self, url)` - Get resource size via HEAD\n- `FetchClient::probe(&mut self, url)` - Check URL accessibility\n\n**Helper:**\n- `FetchClient::extract_provider_from_url(url)` - Extracts provider identifier from URL\n\n**Selection Logic:**\n- No selection logic - executes requests against provided URLs\n- Extracts provider from URL for failure tracking\n\n**`should_reprobe` Integration:** \n- ✅ **FULLY INTEGRATED** - All HTTP methods track failures\n- ✅ Calls `record_failure()` on any HTTP error or non-success status\n- ✅ Calls `record_success()` on successful responses\n- ✅ `should_reprobe()` method (line 464) checks if failures >= threshold\n- ⚠️ **DOES NOT TRIGGER RE-PROBE** - only tracks failures for caller to check\n\n**Failure Tracking Flow:**\n```\nHTTP Request\n    ↓\nSuccess? → NO → record_failure(provider)\n    ↓                    ↓\n   YES                  Check should_reprobe(provider)?\n    ↓                    ↓\nrecord_success(provider)     YES → Caller should trigger re-probe\n```\n\n---\n\n## Runtime Workflow\n\n### Correct Usage Pattern (as documented in `provider_probe.rs`)\n\n```rust\nuse gribtract::ProviderProbe;\nuse gribtract_fetch::probe::ProviderFailureTracker;\nuse std::path::Path;\n\n// 1. Load provider probe results\nlet probe = match ProviderProbe::load(Path::new(\"provider-probe.json\")) {\n    Ok(p) => p,\n    Err(_) => {\n        // File absent - trigger initial probe\n        run_probe_and_write_json();\n        return;\n    }\n};\n\n// 2. Initialize failure tracker\nlet tracker = ProviderFailureTracker::default_threshold();\n\n// 3. Check if we should re-probe (Case 2: stale OR Case 3: consecutive failures)\nif !probe.is_valid(24 * 3600, &tracker) {\n    let needing = probe.providers_needing_reprobe(&tracker);\n\n    if !probe.is_fresh(24 * 3600) {\n        eprintln!(\"provider-probe.json is stale (>24h old), triggering re-probe...\");\n    }\n\n    if !needing.is_empty() {\n        eprintln!(\"Re-probe triggered by consecutive failures: {}\", \n                   needing.join(\", \"));\n    }\n\n    run_probe_and_write_json();\n    return;\n}\n\n// 4. Safe to use cached provider rankings\nif let Some(provider) = probe.best_provider(\"gfs\") {\n    println!(\"Best GFS provider: {provider}\");\n\n    // 5. After HTTP requests, record success/failure\n    match fetch_data_from_provider(provider).await {\n        Ok(_) => {\n            tracker.record_success(provider);\n            println!(\"Successfully fetched from {provider}\");\n        }\n        Err(_) => {\n            let count = tracker.record_failure(provider);\n            eprintln!(\"HTTP error from {provider} (failure {count}/3)\");\n        }\n    }\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## Current Integration Status\n\n### ✅ Fully Integrated Locations\n\n1. **`ProviderProbe::is_valid()` in both crates** - Checks both staleness AND consecutive failures\n2. **`FetchClient` HTTP methods** - All track failures and success correctly\n3. **`ProviderFailureTracker`** - Standalone tracker for use with loaded probe **`ProviderProbe::ranked_providers()`** - Does NOT check failures, assumes pre-validation\n3. **`ProviderProbe::get_best_provider()`** - Does NOT check failures, assumes pre-validation\n\n### ❌ Not
